fixes.fix_explanation: A sitemap.xml tells search engines which pages exist on your site and how often they change, helping Google and Bing discover and index your content faster. Save this file as sitemap.xml and upload it to your domain root, then submit it in Google Search Console.
fixes.fix_location: Save as a new file at https://example-blog.com/sitemap.xml (i.e., the root of your web server, e.g., /var/www/html/sitemap.xml or your CMS's public root folder)

fixes.fix_explanation: A robots.txt file tells search engine crawlers which parts of your site they are allowed to access, and also points them directly to your sitemap for faster discovery. Save this as robots.txt in your domain root alongside sitemap.xml.
fixes.fix_location: Save as a new file at https://example-blog.com/robots.txt (i.e., the root of your web server, e.g., /var/www/html/robots.txt or your CMS's public root folder)

fixes.fix_code:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Blog",
  "name": "The Daily Grind",
  "description": "Explore the world of specialty coffee. Brewing guides, bean reviews, and café culture from around the globe.",
  "url": "https://example-blog.com/",
  "inLanguage": "en",
  "publisher": {
    "@type": "Organization",
    "name": "The Daily Grind",
    "url": "https://example-blog.com/",
    "logo": {
      "@type": "ImageObject",
      "url": "https://example-blog.com/logo.png"
    }
  },
  "about": [
    {"@type": "Thing", "name": "Specialty Coffee"},
    {"@type": "Thing", "name": "Coffee Brewing"},
    {"@type": "Thing", "name": "Café Culture"},
    {"@type": "Thing", "name": "Coffee Bean Reviews"}
  ]
}
</script>
fixes.fix_explanation: JSON-LD structured data helps search engines understand your site's content and can unlock rich results in Google Search, such as enhanced listings with your logo and site details. Place this script block inside your HTML head section, and update the logo URL to point to your actual logo image.
fixes.fix_location: Paste inside the <head> element in your HTML, just before the closing </head> tag
